Q: How to prevent "Operation not supported" exception when making HTTP request from Cloud Run web instance? A:

This looks like the documented .NET 8 SocketsHttpHandler / Alt-Svc regression seen in constrained environments such as Google Cloud, and not like an HttpClientFactory problem. Microsoft fixed it in PR #94861 and backported it to .NET 8 in PR #95123. Disabling HTTP/3 advertisement on the GCP HTTPS frontend is a strong mitigation because it removes the Alt-Svc header that triggers this path. But for this specific case, you still need to verify the actual runtime version running in Cloud Run and confirm the load balancer frontend is no longer advertising HTTP/3, because the asker reported they still saw the problem on 8.0.26

Q: How do I make my Jest tests, runnable in Node.js, compatible with Bun if I am using Babel transform from browser into Node.js-compatible JavaScript? A:

bun test is not Jest running inside Bun. It is a completely separate test runner that happens to understand the Jest API. It uses its own engine and never touches your babel.config.js, so babel-plugin-rewire and export-toplevel never run. That is why tokenizer.tokenize comes back as undefined, your file loads with no exports at all.

You have two practical options that I've checked.

Option 1: keep using Jest, just run it through Bun

Change your package.json test script to call Jest directly, then use bun run test instead of bun test:

json

{ "scripts": { "test": "jest" } }

This runs the full Jest pipeline including Babel transforms. You lose Bun's native speed but nothing else changes.

Option 2: add explicit exports to your source files

Add this at the bottom of tokenizer.js and any other file your tests import:

js

if (typeof module !== 'undefined') {
  module.exports = { tokenize };
}

Bun will load the file as-is and find a real export. In the browser, module is undefined so the line is skipped. Once you do this you can also drop export-toplevel from your Babel config since you no longer need it.
